clue.text: Change course, producing equestrian gear

blocks.note: first meaning: a sailing ship changes direction by turning into the wind
second meaning: saddles, bridles and other riding equipment

explanation.surface: A rider swerves off course and ends up with new riding kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors zigzag against the wind by tacking, and stable equipment such as saddles and bridles is collectively called tack.

clue.text: Print and mould always in similar parts

blocks.note: to type is to put into print
to cast metal is to form it in a mould

explanation.surface: A printer prints and casts metal letters in matching pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like components in a print shop, but it means acting roles.
explanation.definitionFit: A typecast actor is repeatedly given the same sort of role, the meaning of always in similar parts.

clue.text: Easy to understand pay

blocks.note: first meaning: plain, lucid
second meaning: to settle a debt or bill in full

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a description of a simple salary; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucid explanation is clear, and to clear a debt is to pay it off entirely.

clue.text: Work out duty to admit hesitation

indicators.note: to admit is to let something in, so one word takes the other inside itself

blocks.note: excise is a tax levied on goods
the sound a speaker makes when hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone calculates how much tax is owed while allowing for a moment's dithering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' reads as calculate, but the definition is the noun-free verb sense of physical training; EXCISE is a tax on goods such as alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: To work out at the gym is to do physical training, so the two phrases are synonyms as verbs.

clue.text: Spy arranged adverse procedure

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so those letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
OP is short for operation, a surgical procedure

explanation.surface: An agent set up a hostile operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spy' reads as a noun, but here it is the verb: to listen in secretly.
explanation.definitionFit: To eavesdrop is to listen secretly to a private conversation, a way to spy on others.

clue.text: Provide conclusion with cry of pain

blocks.note: the end is the conclusion
what someone says when hurt

explanation.surface: Supply a painful yelp to finish things off.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give money or a quality to someone, so it means to furnish or supply.

clue.text: Order answer and anger door attendant

blocks.note: to commission a work is to order it
A is the abbreviation for answer
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Someone tells a doorman to reply and be furious.
explanation.walkthrough: A commissionaire is a uniformed doorman at a British hotel, cinema or office.
explanation.definitionFit: A commissionaire is a uniformed porter stationed at the entrance of a hotel or theatre.

clue.text: Hotel in predicament over a page showing pile of rubbish

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the word for a tight spot

blocks.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet
being in a scrape is being in trouble
taken as written
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A hotel in trouble with a page reveals a heap of junk.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so the hotel-in-predicament sits before the following letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapheap is a heap of discarded waste and junk, literally a pile of rubbish.

clue.text: Torment parent, embracing naughty role very quickly

indicators.note: embracing means holding in the arms, so the parent word wraps round the mixed letters
naughty means misbehaving, so these letters do not stay in line

blocks.note: hell is torment or suffering
a father is a parent
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A child torments Dad by playing a mischievous part.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell for leather is an idiom for going at breakneck speed, originally of riders on horseback.

clue.text: Kept quiet, not demonstrative

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
a reserved person does not show their feelings

explanation.surface: Someone stayed silent and kept their emotions to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept quiet' looks like a single phrase meaning silent; the definition is only 'Kept'.
explanation.definitionFit: Food or buildings that are kept from decay are preserved, so the past participles match.

clue.text: Unite in reversing your strike

indicators.note: reversing means the following abbreviation is read from its end back to its start

blocks.note: to mar is to damage or spoil, as a blow does
YR is the standard abbreviation for your

explanation.surface: An instruction to join together in turning back an industrial walkout.
explanation.definitionFit: To marry two people or things is to join them together, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Story long devoid of energy

indicators.note: devoid of means lacking, so a letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: to long for something is to yearn
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A tale that goes on and on but has no spark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective describing the story, but it is the verb meaning to desire.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn is an informal word for a tale, often a long rambling or tall one.

clue.text: Song raises crew's help at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: all fifteen letters are used as fodder

explanation.surface: A sea shanty lifts the spirits of sailors who need a hand on board.
explanation.walkthrough: Careless Whisper is George Michael's 1984 hit single; the nautical surface hides the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless Whisper is a famous pop hit by George Michael, so it is one example of a song.

clue.text: Support gullible person in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means we go by how a word is pronounced rather than written

blocks.note: a sucker is someone easily fooled

explanation.surface: Backing for someone credulous who appears in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Succour is help or aid given in time of need, a synonym of support as a noun or verb.

clue.text: Singer with stake in church employment

indicators.note: in places the gambling term inside the two joined words

blocks.note: an ante is a poker player's stake
CH is the abbreviation for church
use is employment, as in the employment of a tool

explanation.surface: A vocalist with a financial interest in a job at church.
explanation.definitionFit: A chanteuse is a female singer, especially one who performs in nightclubs or cabarets.

clue.text: Expected to cover stone with right cloth

indicators.note: to cover something is to go around it, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: something due is expected to arrive
ST is the abbreviation for stone, a British weight of 14 pounds
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Instructions to drape a slab with the proper fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A duster is a piece of soft fabric used to wipe away dust, so it is a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Is suitor initially overwhelmed by awful rejection?

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept
overwhelmed by means engulfed, so the short pieces are swallowed by the adjective

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of suitor
dismal means dreadful or awful

explanation.surface: Is a wooer crushed by being turned down so badly?
explanation.definitionFit: A dismissal is a sending away or refusal, so it is a synonym for rejection.

clue.text: Hairstyle that could have distracted any pilot?

indicators.note: distracted means confused and disturbed, so the following letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the eight letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: A flowing hairdo swinging in the cockpit might put an aviator off.
explanation.definitionFit: A ponytail is hair gathered and tied at the back of the head, a common hairstyle.

clue.text: Delay retreating, then cut and run

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word for delay is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a lag is a delay
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: Stalling, backing off, then deciding to cut and run away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut and run' reads as a single idiom, but 'cut' is wordplay and 'run' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's fastest pace is a gallop, and to gallop is to run fast.

clue.text: Note restricting most of military unit I sign

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so the note holds the rest within it
most of means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: so (soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
a corps is a large army formation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A memo limiting the soldiers of a regiment, which the narrator signs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' looks like a verb for signing the note, but it means a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio, the scorpion, is one of the twelve astrological signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Worker perhaps with loud complaint

blocks.note: a worker is a type of bee, hence 'perhaps'
f (forte) is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: An employee is grumbling noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker' looks like an employee; in crosswords it is often a worker bee.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal speech a beef is a grievance or grumble, so it is a slang synonym for complaint.

clue.text: Remarkably bad error in daily tax

indicators.note: something bad has gone wrong, so the letters that follow are disordered

blocks.note: all fifteen letters are used as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed at a serious mistake in a tax charged every day.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adverbs mean to an unusual or striking degree, so they are interchangeable synonyms.

clue.text: Study variable set

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A maths student studies an unknown quantity that has been fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' sounds like a mathematical set; it means prepared, as in 'ready, steady, go'.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who is set is prepared to start, so set and ready are synonyms as adjectives.

clue.text: One with despondency missing last house

indicators.note: missing last means without its final letter, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
gloom is a state of despondency

explanation.surface: A person who has lost heart now lacks their final home.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped dwelling built from snow blocks, so it is a kind of house.

clue.text: Wealthy level

blocks.note: first meaning: having plenty of money, especially for now
second meaning: perfectly even with an adjoining surface

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a description of one rich person; they are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being flush means having cash to spare, and a surface flush with another sits exactly even with it.

clue.text: Strange rituals held by motoring organisation in country

indicators.note: strange means odd or unfamiliar, so these letters appear in an unusual order
held by means gripped inside, so the jumbled letters sit within the organisation

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
the AA is the Automobile Association, a British breakdown service

explanation.surface: Odd ceremonies are performed by a car club somewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is the Automobile Association, the British equivalent of a motoring club offering roadside help.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is a nation in the southern hemisphere, so it is one example of a country.

clue.text: Disloyalty in university mostly after letter about resistance

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the Greek letter goes round the abbreviation
mostly means not entirely, so the final letter of the name is dropped
after means placed following, so the shortened university comes last

blocks.note: beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
Yale is the American Ivy League university

explanation.surface: Treachery at a college shown in a letter concerning opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayal is the act of breaking faith with someone, so it is a synonym for disloyalty.

clue.text: Declaration of single spirit

indicators.note: a declaration is spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: sole means only or single

explanation.surface: An announcement of a lone ghost or of one unmarried spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: The soul is the immaterial essence of a person, which is also called their spirit.
